newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - Rains to underpin firm SE Asian prices.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Rains to underpin firm SE Asian prices.

text.p: Regional rubber prices will probably rise this week as torrential downpours trim supplies and buying picks up from European dealers returning from their summer vacations, traders said on Monday.
"We feel prices could move up next week as supplies get thinner and thinner because of the wet spell," a dealer at a Malaysian trading firm said.
"We have a feeling that European dealers may start to buy from September as factories are resuming their operations with the summer holidays coming to an end," the dealer added.
Rains continued to drench rubber farms in Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia, hindering tapping and prompting some producers to sell small quantities in the hope of getting higher prices, dealers said.
Dealers said prices came down last week because of a technical correction and a rally was now expected on the back of stronger markets in Indonesia and Thailand.
Dealers in Malaysia said they expected some local and European dealers to inquire for drum latex for September/October shipment. It is quoted at around 248 to 252 Malaysian cents a kg.
Buyers for Malaysia's benchmark October RSS1 were quoted at 329 cents against 330 a week ago and October SMR 20 was at 315.50 cents against 314 cents.
But a Singapore rubber dealer said signs that rains may be easing in Malaysia and Thailand may cut short any surge in prices.

"The weather in those two countries is beginning to improve so the short-term outlook may tend to be bearish. Stocks in Japan are also still quite high and demand remains a bit thin," the trader said.
"People are watching the stocks in Japan closely to see where they will go," a Thai trader in the southern town of Hatyai said, adding prices may dip this week as a result.
Thai rubber prices, which eased last week after buying interest from Japan waned, were also hit by the sidelinining of Chinese buyers who found the prices too high, traders said.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for October shipment was quoted at US$1.26/kg FOB Bangkok from around $1.28/kg last week.
December/January delivery dipped to $1.27-$1.28/kg FOB Bangkok compared with $1.29-$1.30/kg a week earlier.
In Indonesia, prices for benchmark tyre-grade SIR20 were seen staying stable in the coming week, with sentiment expected to remain firm as rains hit supplies, dealers said.
"Sentiment on SIR20 is likely to remain firm, but trading volume is seen on a downtrend after recent active foreign buying," one dealer in the south Sumatran city of Palembang said.

Dealers said SIR20 offer prices for October deliveries were likely to be stable in the range between 56.50-57.50 U.S. cents/lb fob Medan, 56.25-57.25 cents fob Palembang, Surabaya and Padang, and at 56.00-57.00 cents fob Jambi and Pontianak.
Market Sentiment for SIR10, however, was likely to stay soft despite lower supplies, one Jakarta rubber dealer said.

"Demand for SIR10 is likely to stay weak. We have lowered our offer prices to 127.75 cents/kg for November deliveries since several days ago from the previous 128.5 cents, but so far we have no deals done," the dealer said.
Dealers said SIR3L was last traded at 140.0 cents/kg fob Medan for November deliveries against 141.25 previously.
One latex dealer in the west Javanese city of Tangerang said he expected to sell between 175 to 200 tonnes of latex in September against some 150 tonnes in August.
High amoniac latex was on offer at 2,260 rupiah/kg in Tangerang and Bandung against the previous 2,350 rupiah due to weak demand.
(With contributions from Jakarta, Kuala Lumpur and Bangkok)
- Singapore newsroom (65-8703305)
